thread:
Camille: Quick post-launch pulse 1 - assistive completions CTR down ~12% on web, and two enterprise customers reported throughput drops during nightly reports. We need to decide urgent-patch vs backlog. My default: urgent-patch = session loss, data loss, paid-SLA regressions, or clear funnel regression. Everything else -> next iteration. Thoughts?

Omar: From initial triage: (1) long-prompt completions sometimes truncate early due to a server-side OOM guard kicking in, (2) rate-limiter misclassification caused spurious 429s for batched report jobs, (3) embedding freshness for the search index lagging (TTL misapplied). I'd call (1) and (2) urgent. Embedding TTL is important but lower immediate user-facing severity.

Lea: UX note 1: truncation causes missing CTAs in the assistant reply. For a reversible mitigation we can add a client-side display that shows "response truncated, continue?" and cap client-sent max tokens while we patch the server. Low-risk and quick.

Noah: Support queue: Solace and Helios (enterprise) reported 429s during scheduled nightly exports; both flagged as priority accounts and asked for an ETA. They said they'll escalate to their CSMs if we don't target a fix in 24h. Suggest org-targeted rollout to minimize blast.

Isha: QA proposal: acceptance criteria for urgent-patch canary: 
- no session-loss or truncation-related UX regressions in canary for 4h
- error-rate delta <= baseline +0.25% over 2h rolling
- 429s for target orgs reduced to <= baseline +0.1% in canary window
I'll own smoke & regression gating.

BugBot: CI snapshot: 3 failing tests (one new flake in long-prompt integration). Full CI: https://ci.redwood/internal/3199998888. Recommend running focused e2e on long prompts pre-canary.

Camille: Proposed decision: Urgent-patch (this week) = server OOM guard adjustment + better memory path for long prompts (Omar), tighten rate-limiter classification for batch jobs and add org-except list (Omar + Eng-Infra), client-side truncated indicator + cap (Lea). Defer embedding TTL refactor and search reindexing to next sprint. Anyone object?

Omar: No objection. Implementation notes: for rate-limiter we can add an allowlist for known scheduled-job headers and add an org_exempt list for Solace/Helios. Rough estimates: OOM fix ~1.5d, rate-limiter change + tests ~0.75d, allowlist + canary hook ~0.5d.

Lea: I'll ship the client indicator and token-cap change as a quick revert-able flag. Estimate 0.5d. UI snippet to show: "[...truncated] Continue" CTA.

Noah: I'll prepare the targeted customer comms and coordinate CS outreach. We'll only notify Solace/Helios once canary is green.

Camille: Canary rollout plan (org-targeted): 2% -> 20% -> 100% over 3 hours for Solace/Helios, with auto-rollback triggers: any session-loss, truncation UX regressions detected by synthetic checks, or error-rate +0.4% absolute. Example route config: 
```
route_match: org_id in ["solace","helios"]
percent: 2
```

Isha: I'll provision the synthetic checks for truncation and the smoke e2e for long prompts. If the canary meets acceptance criteria after 4h we promote; otherwise auto-rollback and open postmortem.

Omar: Action owners: Omar (OOM long-prompt fix + rate-limiter), Lea (client truncated indicator + flag), Eng-Infra (org canary route + rollback), Noah (customer comms), Isha (QA gating). Target: start canary tomorrow 07:00 UTC.

BugBot: Post-change CI runs queued; will report smoke results to this thread.

Camille: One more note: short-term token-cap may increase server-side token count by ~1.5% due to lost client-side caching. OK trade for stability window?

Omar: OK from engineering side. We'll monitor cost and revert cap when safe.

Noah: :thumbsup: I'll hold the CS messages until canary green.

Lea: :thumbsup:

Isha: On it 1 will post gating results.

Camille: Thanks team. I'll update the board (label tickets urgent-patch) and schedule a 30m status update 2h after the canary starts.
